He who is fierce, who split the mountain-cave, who sent forth the rivers downward; he who placed the cooked [milk] among the cows. ||25|| He who is fierce, who split the mountain-cave, who sent forth the rivers downward; he who placed the cooked [milk] among the cows. ||25||

He [Indra] shattered the *phaliga* cloud for the sake of water—since *phaliga* is listed among the names of clouds in the passage "the *raivata* cloud is the *phaliga*"—and he released the rivers and waters downward from the intermediate space. And he held fast the pure milk within the cows; such is the meaning: that one is Indra. || 5 ||

He slew Vṛtra, O Ṛcīṣama, the son of Urṇavābha, the serpent-swallowing one; he pierced Arbuda with frost. *ahan vṛtram ṛcīṣama aurṇavābham ahīśuvam | himenāvidhyadarbudam || 26 ||* The third hymn, consisting of nineteen verses beginning with "vayaṃ gha tvā," is the work of Medhyātithi Kāṇva.
It is composed primarily in the Bṛhatī meter; the three verses beginning with the sixteenth are Gāyatrīs, and the nineteenth is an Anuṣṭubh.

Indra is the deity. Thus it has been enumerated: “*Vayaṃ gha*, [consisting of] one less than nine [verses], by Medhyātithi, in the Bṛhatī metre, with three Gāyatrīs and ending in an Anuṣṭubh. In the Niṣkevalya of the Mahāvrata, fifteen verses from the beginning of the Bārhatasūkta are used.

Likewise, it is enjoined by Śaunaka in the *Pañcamāraṇyaka*: “One extracts fifteen [verses] beginning with ‘vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvantaḥ’ and the two-footed verse from ‘mo ṣu tvā vāghataścanā’” (*Ai. Ā. 5.2.4*).
On the twenty-fourth day, at the midday pressing (*mādhyandina-savana*), the triplet beginning with ‘vayaṃ gha tvā’ is an optional *stotriya* for the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsin* recitation.
Accordingly, the Sūtra states: “‘vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvantaḥ... ka īṃ veda sute sacā’” (*Āśva. Śr. 7.4*).
The *anurūpa* [verse] must have the same melody as the *ṛc*;
and it is stated in the Sūtra: “‘vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvantaḥ’—these three are *bṛhatī*s” (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 8.5).
In that very *śastra*, “ka īṃ veda” is the optional *anurūpa*.
The Sūtra has already been stated.
O Vṛtra-slayer, we who have pressed the Soma and spread the sacrificial grass sit around you as your praisers at the outpourings of the filter, like waters.
We, O Vṛtrahan, having pressed the soma and trimmed the sacrificial grass, sit around you as your praisers at the outpourings of the filter, like waters. 1.
O Vṛtra-slayer Indra, we indeed—having pressed the Soma, having poured it out—approach you as waters flow down a slope.
At the outpourings of the purifying Soma juices, the singers who have strewn the sacrificial grass sit around you.
The men, the masters, chanting hymns, call upon you when the soma is pressed;
when, O Indra, will you come in thirst to the pressed juice as to your home, like a bellowing bull?

Men, bearing hymns of praise, sing to you at the libation, O Vasu, in their exclusive devotion. When, O Indra, will you come thirsting to the pressed juice as to your home, like a bellowing bull to the flowing water?
O Indra, you who provide a dwelling, the men who offer hymns—leaders who guide—call out to you when the Soma is pressed, at the point of its release.
Moreover, Indra, thirsting for the pressed Soma, like a rushing stream or like a bellowing bull that moves through the forest, making his sound, when will he come to our home, our place of rest?
O bold one, like Kaṇva’s [son], you have revealed the thousandfold wealth;
O Maghavan, O far-seeing one, we quickly implore you for that golden-hued, cattle-filled bounty.

With these songs of Kaṇva’s lineage, boldly strike out for the bull-like one a thousandfold booty. O Maghavan, far-seeing one, we quickly implore you for that wealth of golden hue consisting of cattle.
O bold Indra, for the sake of the Vṛṣṇi, aiming toward the Kaṇvas—
there is a shift in case endings— you have shattered, that is, bestow, thousandfold booty (*vāja*).
O Maghavan, possessor of wealth, O far-seeing Indra, we—being bold—boldly and swiftly (makṣu) beg for and request that which is hated by enemies, a prize consisting of cattle and golden-hued wealth;
"of you two" is the understood sense.

1. In manuscripts *ga*, *gha*, *ta*, *na*, and *bha*, the word *medhyātithi* is absent. 2. In manuscripts *ga*, *ta*, *na*, and *bha*, the word *indra* is absent. 3. In manuscript *gha*, it reads *paryāyate upāsate*. 4. In manuscripts *ga*, *ta*, and *na*, the word *ukthinaḥ* is absent. 5. In manuscripts *ga*, *ta*, *na*, and *bha*, the word *dehi* is absent.

Drink, O Medhyātithi; sing for Indra in the exhilaration of the juice! He who is joined with his two bay steeds, who is present at the pressed soma, the wielder of the thunderbolt whose chariot is golden. Drink! Sing! In the exhilaration of the juice—for that Indra—O Medhyātithi! He who is joined with his two bay steeds in his own chariot; who is present at the pressed soma as a companion; Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose chariot is golden.
He who is easily invoked, who is most skillful, the lord who is wise in his quality,
he who is the source of light.

When the Soma has been pressed, who knows this Indra as he drinks the Soma together with the truthful priests? No one knows him—this is the meaning. Or what word does he hold? This Indra, with powerful jaws, exhilarated by the food of Soma, shatters the fortresses with his might and strength. Like a wild elephant in rut, he assumes his course in many places. No one can restrain you; come to the pressed juice! Great, you move with power. (8) *Like a wild beast, like an elephant in rut, he assumes his course in many places.* No one can restrain you; come to the pressed juice! Great, you move with power. (8) A "wild beast" (*mṛga*) is one who seeks out enemies; an "elephant" (*vāraṇa*) is like one that exudes rut-fluid (*dānā*). In many sacrifices, Indra maintains his intoxication, which is characterized by its movement. Now follows a direct praise: O Indra, no one can restrain you. Come to the pressed Soma! Great, you move with power. (8)
O Maghavan, your *abhīśavas*—the reins, the horse-bridles—are *vṛṣaṇas*, i.e., showerers [of benefits].
The golden (*hiraṇyayī*) *kakṣā* (the leather thong) is also a *vṛṣan*;
the chariot (*ratha*) too is a *vṛṣan*, a showerer.
The two bay horses are also "vṛṣaṇā," meaning the two "vṛṣaṇau," the two showerers.
O Śatakratu, Indra of manifold wisdom, you too are "vṛṣā," the showerer.
Let the bull presser press for you; O you of bull-like vigor, bring [the offering].
The bull has flowed, the bull into the rivers, for you, the one who stands over the tawny steeds.
The bull, the impeller—let him press for you! O bull, O Ṛjīpin, bring it hither! The bull has flowed into the rivers for the bull; for you, O driver of the bay steeds. 12.
O *vṛṣan*, raining Indra, let the presser, being himself a showerer (*vṛṣan*), press out the Soma for you; as one who pours forth, let him pour it out.
O *ṛjīpin*, Indra of straight course, bring wealth to us; bring it hither!
O *sthātar* Indra, standing before the bay horses (*harīṇām aśvānām*), the showerer has held out the showering Soma for you in the rivers, in the waters, for the sake of the sacrifice.
O most powerful one, come to Indra to drink the sweet Soma;
let the bountiful Maghavan, the wise one, hear this as he approaches these great hymns.

O Indra, come for the drinking of the sweet Soma juice, O most powerful one! This Maghavan, who is rich in wisdom, hears our songs; he comes toward us for the sacred prayer and the hymns of praise. 13.
O most powerful, O most mighty Indra, come hither for the drinking of the *somya*—the honey-like nectar consisting of Soma. Why must you come? He says:

because without your coming, this Indra—the possessor of wealth (*maghavan*), the one of good deeds (*sukratuḥ*) or excellent wisdom—does not listen to our songs (*giraḥ*), praises (*stutīḥ*), sacred prayers (*brahma*), hymns (*ukthāni*), or invocations (*accha*). He does not hear them.
Therefore, the meaning is "coming."
Let the bay steeds yoked to the chariot carry you, who stand upon the chariot;
O Śatakratu, slayer of Vṛtra, pass even through the obstacles of others.
Let the bay steeds, yoked to the chariot, carry you who stand upon the chariot; O Vṛtra-slayer, O Śatakratu, pass even through the obstructions of others. 14.

O Vṛtra-slayer, O Śatakratu of manifold wisdom, you who stand upon the chariot—the Lord who is the goal of the chariot—may your bay horses, yoked to the chariot, passing over the libations that belong to others, bring hither our own libations.
O Most Mighty One, accept today our final hymn of praise;
may all our offerings be most auspicious for your exhilaration, O celestial Soma-drinker.
1. Kha-ta-na-bha-śa-ṛjīpin; 2. Gha-śastrāṇi ca; 3. Ga-gha-ta-na-bha-accha; 4. Gha-jña-ta-tiraścit.

O you who are swift as a deer, accept our hymn today at its conclusion! O most bounteous one, pour it out for us! May all these exhilarations be most auspicious for your joy; O drinker of Soma, let them yield for you. 15.
O you who are the greatest of the great, the supreme object of worship, today accept and hold fast our most proximate hymn of praise, we who are worthy guests.
O radiant one, drinker of Soma, may these libations of ours be most auspicious, most pleasant for your exhilaration, O Indra.
For this secret instruction of yours does not delight another, O Hero, who has brought us here. 16 For that secret instruction of yours does not please anyone else, O Hero, who has led us hither. 16

That hero, that warrior who brought us here—he is Indra; he takes no pleasure, indeed does not delight, in your instruction or command. He takes no pleasure in my instruction or command either, nor does he take pleasure in the instruction of anyone else.
However, the meaning is that he delights solely in protection.

Even Indra himself declared this: "The mind of a woman is unteachable, and her impulse is indeed fleeting. (17) Even Indra himself declared this: the mind of a woman is unteachable, and her impulse is indeed fleeting. (17)
He who was the giver of wealth to Medhyātithi became a man after having been a woman; he was Dyāyogirāsaṅga.
Then, that which Indra said, he speaks here.
And so they say: “Dyāyogirāsaṅga, who, having been a woman, became a man, gave a gift to Medhyātithi.”
Even Indra himself, indeed, said this:
"The mind and thought of women cannot be governed by a man; they are impossible to discipline because of their inherent strength.
Moreover, he spoke of a woman's *ṛtu*—her wisdom—as being *raghu*, meaning swift or fleeting.

Even though they are a pair, both distilling exhilaration, they draw the chariot together; yet the yoke of the Bull alone is higher. 18. Even though they are a pair, both distilling exhilaration, they draw the chariot together; yet the yoke of the Bull alone is higher. 18.
Even the two horses of Indra, though they flow with intoxication, indeed go toward him; as a pair, they carry the chariot of Indra alone.
Even so, even thus, the yoke-pole of the bull Indra’s chariot is higher than that of the two horses.

Look downward, not upward; draw your feet closer together. Let them not see your bare calves, for you have become a Brahmin woman. 19. Look downward; not upward; more closely; draw your two feet; let them not see your bare calves; for you have indeed become a Brahmin woman. 19.
Thus Indra, coming from the intermediate space, spoke to Dyāyogī, who was a woman desiring manhood for herself regarding the chariot. He said: "O Dyāyogī, being what you are, look downward;
this is the duty of women."

Do not look upward. 1. [The syllables] ga, ta, na, and bha are predominant. 2. The pair gha and the two pairs [of syllables]. 3. In the application of gha; in the application of ta3; in the application of ta4, na, bha1, and bha2. 4. Ga-paśya.
Indeed, looking upward is not the duty of women.
O Hara, draw your two feet even closer together so that they are joined;
the meaning is that you, as a woman, must not stand with your feet placed apart as a man does. Furthermore, [draw] your calves...
What is "kaśca-kaśca-kaśakau"?
The word *kaśā* denotes the act of striking with a whip.
May both these limbs, the *kaśakau*, not be seen; may men not behold them.
The non-visibility of those two [the private parts] occurs through the proper wearing of the garment;
therefore, wear the garment properly.
For women are completely covered even to their secret parts—this is the meaning.
For indeed, because of this reason, you have become a woman equal to Bhaṅgā.
The fourth hymn, consisting of eighteen verses beginning with "indra yāhi," is the seerly composition of Nipātiti Kāṇva; it is in the Anuṣṭubh meter.
The sixteenth verse consists of three Gāyatrīs.
These [seers] are the Vasurocis Aṅgirasas.
The *sahasrasaṃsthākā* [hymns] consist of those three beginning with “ā yadindraśca”; their seers are the Ṛṣis; Indra is the deity.

Thus says the *Anukramaṇī*: “‘endra yāhi’—[these] two less [one] are in the *Anuṣṭubh* meter; another triplet is in the *Gāyatrī* meter; that [collection] of a thousand [verses] was seen by the Vasurocis Aṅgirasas.”
The application is indicated by the indicative mark.
Come to Indra with your bay steeds to the fair praise of Kaṇva;
from yonder heaven you rule, O ye who have gone to heaven, O you whose wealth is the light of heaven!
Come hither, O Indra, with your bay horses to the beautiful hymn of Kaṇva. From yonder heaven, you who rule over that heaven, you have gone to heaven, O Divāvasu, O Divāvasu! 1.
O Indra, come with your tawny horses to the beautiful hymn of praise of Kaṇva;
[come] from heaven—
the sixth case used in the sense of the accusative.
"Under the command of that Indra, he rules over that [place];
there is a shift in case endings.
Therein we dwell in happiness."
O Indra, dweller of the day, you whose oblation is radiant, go to heaven, to the celestial realm—you all go;
the plural number is used for honor.
Or else:
O you who dwell by day, O shakers of heaven, making such-and-such a person's world subject to your command, go you to the divine heaven!
Here, the plural number is used for the sake of honor; this is the meaning.
May the pressing-stone, speaking here as it holds the Soma, draw you hither with its sound;
from the command of that heaven, come to heaven, O you who dwell in the light of heaven!
May the Soma-pressing stone, speaking here, draw you hither with its sound. To that heaven of the Ruler, go ye, O ye who dwell in light! 2.
O Indra, may the pressing-stone—the stone for crushing Soma—here at this sacrifice, being possessed of Soma and making a sound by uttering a noise, bring you here along with its resonance.
The rest is self-evident.
Here, like a wolf shaking its prey, he shakes the spokes of these [chariots];
you who, ruling from yonder heaven, have gone to heaven, O you whose wealth is the light of heaven!
Here the rim of their wheel shakes the sheep like a wolf; from that heaven of the Ruler you have gone to heaven, O Divāvasu, O Divāvasu! 3.

1. Those belonging to the lineage of Taṅnamavasumattocinaṅgiro; 2. of the ṛṣi named Kha-jña-ta-bhara-kaṇva; 3. come (āyāhi) from Bha; 4. while he rules (śāsati); 5. make the heaven (divam) [prosperous] (taṅnam); 6.
of those ruling the world (lokam) Kha-ta-na-bhara—at this sacrifice (vatre), the Soma-creeper (vnemiḥ) of those who are raining down (abhivarṣamāṇānām) vibrates (vibhūnute) intensely;
like a wolf (vṛkaḥ) toward a ewe (urām).
The rest is established.
Kaṇva calls upon you for protection; they call upon you for the winning of booty. Praising that very heaven, go to heaven, O you who have heaven as your wealth!

Ā tvā kaṇva iha arvase havante vājasātaye | diva amuṣya śāṃsato divaṃ yaya divāvaso || 4 || O Indra, here at this sacrifice, the Kaṇvas call upon you for protection and for the acquisition of food; they invoke you directly. The rest is established [as explained elsewhere].
I offer to you, the bull, the first draught of the pressed juices, as one praises that heaven;
go to heaven, O you who dwell in the light of heaven!
I offer to you, the bull among the pressed juices, that foremost draught as if for the sake of heaven; praise that very heaven!

Come to heaven, you who are praised by Manu as the appointed Hotṛ-priest, you who are to be magnified among the gods; praise that very heaven! Come to heaven, O you who provide aid by day, O Divāvasu! 8.
O Indra, may Agni—the invoker to be praised among the gods (*devatrā*), the one who summons the gods, and who has been established by men in their homes—bring you hither.
The rest is self-evident.
May your two bay steeds, dripping with exhilaration, carry you hither like two wings carrying a hawk—
from that heaven where you rule, O Lord of Heaven, you who dwell in light!
May the two bay steeds, distilling exhilaration, carry you hither like two wings a falcon; from that heaven of the ruler, come to heaven, O Divāvasu, O Divāvasu! 9.
O Indra, those two bay horses (*harī*) of yours, which cause the intoxication of enemies to fall away (*madacyutā*), [carry] you like a hawk (*śyenam*), as one's own two wings carry a hawk.

Come from the mountains; come from the summit of the ocean; come from that heaven which rules over heaven, O you who possess splendor by day! 13 Come! From the mountains! From the summit of the ocean! From that heaven which rules over heaven! O you whose wealth is light by day! 13 O Indra, come from the mountains; come hither. Come also from the summit of the ocean—that is, from the firmament. The rest is self-evident.

O Hero, disclose for us thousands of cattle, thousands of horses—those things beneficial as cattle or in the form of cattle, and those beneficial as horses or in the form of horses—from that heaven which commands, from heaven itself, O Lord of Radiant Wealth! O Hero Indra, you must disclose—that is, open up—for us thousands, by the count of thousands, of cattle-beneficial things, either in the form of cattle or beneficial to horses, or consisting of horses themselves. The rest is self-evident.
Bring to us thousands, tens of thousands, and hundreds from yonder heaven; O you whose command is supreme! [Aitareya Āraṇyaka 5.3.6] Sixth Aṣṭaka, 719.
When those swift, agile,
and fleet-footed steeds,
like pigeons in their flight, had been accepted as gifts, [the poet] speaks of a thousand Vasurocis within the midst of the forest.
"By Abhinnendra": this is the fifth hymn, consisting of twenty-four verses, whose seer is Śyāvāśva Ātreya.
Regarding this, the Anukramaṇikā states: "Abhinnā; twenty-four verses; Śyāvāśva; addressed to the Aśvins; of the Upariṣṭājjyotis type; ending with a Paṅkti and five Mahābṛhatīs.
Thus, the meter is Upariṣṭājjyotis.
Because the fourth foot consists of eight syllables; its characteristic is stated in the *Anuvāka* (9.8): "Where there are eight, there is light. The twenty-second [verse] is a *paṅkti*.
The twenty-third is a Mahābṛhatī, because it possesses the characteristics stated in [Anuvāka] 9.9: "A Mahābṛhatī consists of four octosyllabic feet and one dodecasyllabic foot.
The twenty-fourth is a Paṅkti;
its deity is the Aśvins.
In the *asuryāma* [sacrifice], the Hotṛ has an additional hymn, namely this *sūkta* beginning with "abhinnendreṇa.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "The *abhinnendreṇa* [hymn] is to be used for the *bhāvya* [offering]" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 9.11).
O Aśvins, inseparable from Indra, Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus;
being in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, drink the soma together.
Indivisible from Indra, Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus; being ever-present together and in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya—O Aśvins, drink the Soma! 1.
O Aśvins, you two who are co-existent with Indra, Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus; who are in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya—drink the Soma together.
With all prayers, with the world, O possessors of vigor, together with heaven, earth, and the mountains; being in harmony with the Dawn and the Sun, drink the Soma, O Aśvins!

With all prayers, with the world, O you who possess strength, with heaven, with earth, with the pressing-stones, together with the ever-present Dawn and Sūrya—O Aśvins, being of one accord, drink the Soma! 2.

O Aśvins, you two who possess strength through your steeds, drink the Soma together with all our prayers and insights, with the entire world of living beings, with heaven, with earth, with the mountains, and joined together with Dawn and the Sun.
O Aśvins, together with all the gods— the three times eleven Maruts— and in the company of the Bhṛgus, being in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, drink the Soma.

With all the gods, with the three sets of eleven, here with the pressing-stones, with the Maruts, and with the Bhr̥gus—being together with them, being in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya—drink the Soma, O Aśvins! 3.

O Aśvins, together with all the gods—the thirty-three, the thrice eleven—along with the Maruts and the Bhṛgus at this sacrifice, being companions and united with Dawn and Sūrya, drink the soma, you two.

1. Kha-ta-na-bha-1-2-śa-satsu: *vanaspatayaḥ* (O lords of the forest). 2. Ga-jha-ta4-tapovanasya: [of] the grove of asceticism (*tapovana*). 3. Bha3-ca sajoṣasau: [the two] who are in harmony (*sajoṣasau*). 4. Kha-gha-ta-na-bha-sahabhūtī: "O you two who possess common power" (*sahabhūtī*); "you two who are in harmony" (*yuvāṃ sajoṣasā*). 5. Kha-gha-ta-na-bha- 'saṃgatī yuvāṃ': "you two who are united" (*saṃgatī yuvāṃ*) does not exist. 720. Ṛgveda [Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 3, Varga 15].

May you two enjoy the sacrifice; be mindful of my invocation. O two gods, come here to all the libations. In joyful union with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, bring nourishment to us. 4. May you two enjoy the sacrifice; be mindful of my invocation. O two gods, come here to all the libations. In joyful union with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, bring nourishment to us. O Aśvins, may you two enjoy (juṣethām) the sacrifice. Be mindful of (bodhatam) my call (harvasya). Come down to (ava gacchatam) all the libations (viśvā savanā) here at this sacrifice. O Aśvins, being in joyful union (sajorṣā) with Uṣas and Sūrya, bring (voḷaham) food (irpam) to us.

May you both enjoy the hymn of praise, like two youths enjoying the call of a maiden. O two Gods, come here to all the libations at this sacrifice. Being in harmony with the Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, bring us nourishment. O Aśvins, O two Gods, may you both enjoy the *stoma* (hymn of praise) here in this sacrifice; just as two youths enjoy the calling of a maiden, so [should you]. Come here to all the *savanā* (libations) at this sacrifice. The rest is established.

O two gods, may you take pleasure in our songs; may you take pleasure in the sacrifice. O two gods, come here to all the libations. Being in harmony with the Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, bring hither that which is desirable for us. O two gods, Aśvins, may you enjoy (juṣethām) our songs (giraḥ)—that is, our praises—and likewise enjoy (juṣethām) the sacrifice (adhvaram). Come down (ava gacchatam) to all the libations (viśvā savanā) here at this sacrifice. Being in harmony (sajorṣā) with the Dawn (uṣasā) and with the Sun (sūryeṇa), O Aśvins, bring (voḷham) to us that which is desirable (irpam).

Like two *hāridrava* birds, you fly toward the woods; like two buffaloes, you descend toward the pressed Soma. United with Uṣas and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, come three times to our dwelling. O Aśvins, you two fly toward the pressed Soma like two *hāridrava* birds fly toward the woods—“woods” (*vana*) being listed among the names for water—and just as two thirsty buffaloes descend toward water, so do you descend toward the pressed Soma. Joined with Uṣas and with Sūrya, come three times to our dwelling.

1. In the manuscripts *ga*, *ta*, *na*, and *bha*, "viśvā" does not appear before "yajñe. 2. In manuscript *jha*, it reads "āgacchantu"; in *ta* 1, 2, 4, *na*, and *bha* 1, 2, it reads "āgacchanti"; in *ta* 3, "hāgacchanti"; and in *bha* 3, "āgacchatam. 3. In *jha*, *ta* 1, 2, *na*, and *bha* 1, it reads "viśvā viśvāni. 4. In manuscript *gha*, it reads "hāridraveva. 5. In manuscript *gha*, it reads "nyudakādi. 6. In manuscript *gha*, it reads "mahiṣeva. 7. In *ta* and *bha* 1, 2, it reads "trimārga. [Maṇḍala 8, Adhyāya 5, Sūkta 35] Sixth Aṣṭaka: 721.

Like two swans you fly; like two travelers on the road, you go toward the pressed Soma; like two buffaloes, you hasten to the water. Being of one accord with Uṣas and with Sūrya, come thrice, O Aśvins, by this path. O Aśvins, like two swans, and like two travelers on the road who go toward water, so do you fly swiftly toward the pressed Soma. The rest is self-evident.

Like two hawks you fly for the sake of receiving the oblation; like two buffaloes, you go toward the pressed Soma. Being of one accord with the Dawn and with the Sun, come three times today, O Aśvins, with your most excellent chariot. O Aśvins, like two hawks—just as two hawks go through the sky—so do you fly with speed for the sake of receiving the oblation (havyadāṃtaye) for the sake of the sacrificer (yajamāna), toward the pressed Soma. The rest is self-evident.

Drink and be satisfied; come hither and bestow offspring and wealth. Being in harmony with the Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, grant us vigor. (10) Drink! And be satisfied! And come hither! Bestow progeny! And grant us wealth! Being in harmony with the Dawn and with the Sun, O Aśvins, grant us strength. (10) O Aśvins, you two drink the Soma and be satisfied—be satiated for the sake of drinking—and come hither. Having drunk the Soma and being satisfied, may you both sustain us with progeny. Grant us wealth and riches. Being united with the Dawn and with the Sun, grant us vigor and power.

Victorious and spreading forth, protect us and bestow upon us progeny and wealth; being in harmony with the Dawn and the Sun, O Aśvins, grant us vigor. O Aśvins, you two conquer the enemies; spread forth and protect the worshippers and us as well. The rest is self-evident.
Slay our enemies and protect our friends; bestow upon us offspring and wealth.
Being of one mind with Dawn and Sūrya, O Aśvins, grant us vigor.
1. *kha-gha-ta-śa-pathiyāgu* | 2. *ga-gha-ta-na-bha-gacchataṃ ca*. Ṛgveda 3.46.

Strike down our enemies, O Aśvins; go forth to those who are allied with us. Bestow upon us progeny and bestow wealth. Being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, grant us nourishment, O Aśvins. (12) O Aśvins, you two strike down our enemies; and furthermore, go forth to those who are allied with us. The rest is self-evident. (15)

Accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa, and likewise accompanied by Dharma and the Maruts, you two come to the invocation of the singer. Being of one accord with Uṣas, with Sūrya, and with the Ādityas, come hither, O Aśvins! Accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa; and also; accompanied by Dharma; accompanied by the Maruts; of the singer; you two go; to the invocation; being of one accord; with Uṣas; and with Sūrya; and with the Ādityas; come; O Aśvins! And furthermore, O Aśvins, you two—accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa, joined with Mitra and Varuṇa; accompanied by Dharma, joined with Dharma; and accompanied by the Maruts, joined with the Maruts—[come] to the singer's hymn.
O Aśvins, you two, quicken the *brahman* and the Brahmin;
and also quicken our thoughts and our ritual acts;
and protect the trees.
Drive away the diseases and the Rākṣasas;
united with the sun, drink the Soma of the sacrificer who presses it.
Quicken the field and quicken the men; slay the Rākṣasas and drive away the diseases.

O Aśvins, you two gladden the ruling power and the kṣatriya; and furthermore, gladden the men, the warriors. The rest is established.
Quicken the cow and quicken the people; slay the demons and drive away diseases. O Aśvins, being in harmony with Dawn and with Sūrya, [protect] those who press the Soma.
The cow; quicken.

Like reins, O Aśvins, who cause exhilaration to flow, come hither to the sacrifices of Śyāvāśva as he presses the soma; being in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, come across the day. O Aśvins, like reins, come hither to the sacrifices of Śyāvāśva as he presses the soma—ye who cause exhilaration to flow; being in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, come across the day. (21) "O Aśvins, come hither to my sacrifices, which are like reins—that is, just as one holds the reins of a chariot—come near. The rest is established.

Turn your chariot hither; drink the Soma-mead. Come, O Aśvins; arrive! I, destitute of wealth, call upon you both. Bestow treasures upon the donor. O Aśvins, turn your chariot hither toward us; restrain it [in our direction]. Drink the Soma-mead, the essence of Soma. Come to the sacrifice; come toward the Soma. I, Śyāvāśva, desiring protection, call upon you both. Grant treasures to me, the one who offers oblations.

O Aśvins, leaders, come hither for the drinking of the exhilarating [Soma] at this sacrifice where the proclamation of homage has been made; come, approach! I, lacking wealth, invoke you both; bestow treasures upon the donor. O Aśvins, O leaders, come hither for the drinking of the exhilarating [Soma] at this sacrifice where the proclamation of homage has been made. That which is recited for the sake of homage is the *namovāka*; at that sacrifice, thus says the Brāhmaṇa: "Both together indeed constitute the sacrifice: the *sūktavāka* and the *namovāka*" (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.9.1.4). Come for the drinking, that is, for the consumption of Soma. The rest is self-evident.

Satisfy yourselves with the pressed juice, O two Gods, with the food over which *svāhā* has been uttered. Come hither, O Aśvins; approach! Deprived of wealth, I call upon you both; bestow treasures upon the donor. O two Gods, Aśvins, satisfy yourselves with the pressed, consecrated *andhas* (the Soma juice). [The rest is established. 17.
1. O Aśvins, you two who cause the intoxication to flow—meaning you two who cause the pride of enemies to fall away—for the one who presses the soma;
2. [for the sake of] the sacrifices (adhvara), that is, the rituals;
3. [of the one] whose nature is to carry (vahana-śīla); according to Śa, [of the one] whose nature is to see (darśana-śīla).

Begetter of heaven, begetter of earth, drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu! That portion which they have set apart for you—you who conquer all armies, the wide-conquering one, winner of the waters—O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, lord of heroes! O Indra, you are the begetter of heaven; you are the begetter of earth. The rest is established [as explained above].

You are the progenitor of horses, you are the progenitor of cattle; drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu! [Drink] that portion which they have set apart for you—you who conquer all hostile armies, the wide-conquering one, the winner of waters—O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, Lord of heroes! You are the progenitor of horses; you are the progenitor of cattle. The rest is established.

O wielder of the thunderbolt, make the hymn of the Atris great; drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu! [Drink] that portion which they have set apart for you—you who conquer all armies, the wide-conquering one, the winner of waters—O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, Lord of heroes. O wielder of the thunderbolt (*adrivaḥ*), make the hymn of the Atris great (*mahaḥ kṛdhi*)—that is, render it honored. The rest is established [as explained].

Listen to Śyāvāśva as he presses the Soma, just as you listened to Atri while he was performing his rites. O Indra, you alone protected Trasadasyu in the battle for men, strengthening him with sacred prayers (*brahmāṇi*). O Indra, listen to me, Śyāvāśva, who am pressing the Soma and performing my rites, just as you listened to Atri while he was performing his rites. Furthermore, you alone, O Indra, strengthening the sacred prayers (*brahmāṇi*) with desires in the battle for men, protected Trasadasyu.
The seventh hymn, consisting of seven verses beginning with “*predaṃ brahma*,” is the seerly work of Śyāvāśva Ātreya. The first two verses are *jagatī*s of twelve syllables;
the remaining six verses are *mahāpaṅkti*s.
Indra is the deity.
Thus it has been enumerated: "Pre daṃ mahāpāṅktam āghātijagatī."
In the Mahāvrata, this hymn belongs to the Niṣkevalya [Śastra].
And so says the Sūtra: "predaṃ brahmaṇvo madāya" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 7.12).

You have protected this prayer in the battles against Vṛtra; O Indra, Lord of Might, protect the one who presses the juice with all your succours. O Slayer of Vṛtra, drinker of Soma, wielder of the thunderbolt, come now and drink of the Soma at the midday libation.

O Śacīpati Indra, you, in the contests against Vṛtra and in battles, protect—extend your protection with all aids and defenses—to this prayer and to these Brāhmaṇas. And protect those sacrificers who perform the pressing of Soma. Furthermore, O blameless one, O vajra-wielder, O slayer of Vṛtra, O Indra, drink the Soma belonging to the midday libation.
O Indra, Lord of Might, with all your protections, overcome the fierce assailants in battle who seek to harm us.

O Indra, Lord of Might, you rule over both security and exertion with all your protections. O Slayer of Vṛtra, wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of this entire midday soma without fail. kṣemasya ca prayujaśca tvamīśiṣe śacīpata indra viśvābhirūtibhiḥ | mādhyaṃdinasya sarvasya vṛtrahannedha piba somasya vajrivaḥ || 5 || And you, O Indra, Lord of Power, rule over both peace and active endeavor through all your aids. O slayer of Vṛtra, O wielder of the thunderbolt, do not withhold; drink of the midday soma.
Moreover, O Śacīpati Indra, you are the lord (īśiṣe) of the welfare (kṣema) and the acquisition (prayuj) of the entire world— that is to say, of both security and prosperity.
The rest is established.

For the sake of dominion you protect; yet you have not protected us, O Indra, Lord of Might, with all your aids. O Slayer of Vṛtra, drink of the entire midday Soma, O wielder of the thunderbolt, without hesitation. For the sake of dominion— you— protect; not— you— have protected— O Lord of Might, Indra—with all— aids. Of the midday— of the whole— O Slayer of Vṛtra— without hesitation— drink— of the Soma— O wielder of the thunderbolt.
O Indra, Lord of Śacī, you exist for the sovereignty and the strength of the world;
you protect—that is, you guard—those who have taken refuge in you. You, being hidden by us, are not protected by anyone else.
The rest is established.

Listen likewise to the deeds of the chanting Iyāvāśva, just as you listened to those of Atri while he performed his rites. You alone, O Indra, protected Trasadasyu, bringing him forth as one who is invincible, increasing his princely powers. (7) Listen likewise to the deeds of the chanting Iyāvāśva, just as you listened to those of Atri while he performed his rites. You alone, O Indra, protected Trasadasyu, bringing him forth as one who is invincible, increasing his princely powers. (7)
O Indra, as you heard the praise and the deeds of Rebha, of my own Īyāvāśva who performs his rites, and as you heard Atri, so hear me now.
Furthermore, increasing the powers and strengths of the nobles according to their desires, you alone protected Trasadasyu in battle.
The hymn beginning with "yajñasya hi," consisting of ten verses, is the seerly composition (*ārṣa*) of Iyāvāśva; it is in the *gāyatrī* meter and has Indra and Agni as its deities (*devatā*).
Thus it is enumerated: "yajñasya daśaindrāgnam.
This hymn serves as the insertion (*āvāpa*) for the Acchāvāka priest during the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) of the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava Ṣaḍahas.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "For you two belong to the sacrifice; [this is] for the Acchāvāka" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 7.5).
On the twenty-fourth day, at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*), the triplet known as the *ṣaḍaha-stoma-traya* begins with "For you two belong to the sacrifice.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "O Indra and Agni, you two; for you two belong to the sacrifice; [this is] for the Acchāvāka, the priest" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 7.2).
In the Agniṣṭoma, at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*), the *prasthitayājyā* for the Acchāvāka priest is "prātaryāvabhir ahaḥ.
This is prescribed in the Sūtra: "He sacrifices with 'prātaryāvabhiḥ'" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 5.7).
At the twenty-fourth-day rite (*cāturviṃśika*), at the morning pressing, the *paryāsa-stotra* for the Acchāvāka is "iyāvāśvasya."
It is indeed stated elsewhere regarding the multi-day sacrificial sessions (*ahargaṇa*), specifically concerning the second and subsequent desired days:
"The *paryāsa* [hymns] are the three-verse hymns beginning with 'iyāvāśvasya sunvataḥ'" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 7.2).

For you two are the officiating priests of the sacrifice, the chanters at the rites for the sake of booty; O Indra and Agni, take heed of that! 1. For you two are the officiating priests of the sacrifice, the chanters at the rites for the sake of booty; O Indra and Agni, take heed of that! 1.
1. There is no [reading] "ga-ta-na-bha- 'kṣatrāṇi...vardhayan" (increasing the kṣatriyas...).

O Indra and Agni, you two, pure friends, are indeed the two officiating priests (*ṛtvijau*) of the sacrifice. O Indra and Agni, who stand ready for battles and for ritual acts, take note of me—that person—and know my hymn of praise. O Indra and Agni, you who are destroyers (*tośasā*), who travel on chariots (*rathayāvānā*), slayers of Vṛtra (*vṛtrahanā*), and unconquered (*aparājitā*), take note of me—that person. O Indra and Agni, men have milked this exhilarating honey-sweet Soma for you with the pressing-stones. O Indra and Agni, take note of that. Enjoy the sacrifice for the sake of the offering; enjoy the pressed Soma, O you who share the same praise. O Indra and Agni, O leaders (*narā*), come hither! Enjoy these libations (*savanā*) by which you carry the offerings. O Indra and Agni, O leaders, come hither! Enjoy this beautiful hymn of mine, which follows the path of the *Gāyatrī* meter. O Indra and Agni, O leaders, come hither! Come with the gods who travel at dawn, O you whose wealth is to be won, O Indra and Agni, for the drinking of Soma. Hear the call of Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice, O Indra and Agni, for the drinking of Soma. (Note: In verse 8, the word "yebhiḥ" does not appear in some recensions.)

O Indra and Agni, hear the invocation of Śyāvāśva, who is pressing the Soma, and that of the Atris—the officiating priests—for the drinking of the Soma. 8. O Indra and Agni, you two, hear the call of me, Śyāvāśva, the sacrificer who is pressing the Soma, and that of the Atris, for the sake of drinking the Soma.

Thus, O Indra and Agni, I call upon you both for aid, just as the wise have called upon you for the drinking of Soma. (9) O Indra and Agni, just as the wise ones have invoked you both for protection, so do I invoke you for aid and for the drinking of Soma. (9)

I choose the protection of Indra and Agni, who are accompanied by Sarasvatī, for by them the Gāyatra is sung. (10) "I" (āham), "of the two [deities] accompanied by Sarasvatī" (sarasvatīvatoḥ), "of Indra and Agni" (indrāgnyoḥ), "the protection" (avaḥ), "I choose" (vṛṇe), "by whom" (yābhyām), "the Gāyatra" (gāyatram), "is sung" (ṛcyate). (10) For the sake of those two, Indra and Agni, by whom the Gāyatra Sāman is sung—that is, praised—I choose the protection, the aid, belonging to those two Indra and Agni who are accompanied by Sarasvatī, that is, who possess praise. (21) The ninth hymn, consisting of ten verses beginning with "abhi stomi," is the seerage of Nābhāka Kāṇva. Six verses are in the Mahāpaṅkti meter; Agni is the deity. It is recorded: "abhi stomi... Nābhāka [is the seer]; it belongs to Atri; it is indeed in Mahāpaṅkti. The application [of the hymn] is indicated by its internal characteristics.

I have praised Agni, the one worthy of hymns; I laud Agni so that he may be worshipped. May Agni anoint the gods for us. For as a seer (*kavi*), he moves between both worlds, performing his mission as a messenger. May all others, the enemies, perish! I have praised—meaning I extol—the one worthy of hymns, Agni. Furthermore, I laud him with praise (*īḷā*) so that he may be worshipped. Moreover, may Agni anoint the gods for us with oblations at the *vidatha*, the sacrifice. As a seer who perceives all things, he moves between both [worlds], heaven and earth, performing the work of a messenger characterized by carrying the oblations. May all others—even the enemies—perish; let them all be destroyed. The root *nabh* signifies the act of harming; let them be harmed by Agni.
