O Agni, I offer these prayers to you like clarified butter into your mouth; as such, make them known among the gods, for you are the ancient, auspicious messenger of Vivasvat. May all others who are alike perish! 3 O Agni, [I offer] these prayers to you; indeed, I pour them like clarified butter into your mouth. As such, make them known among the gods, for you are the ancient, auspicious messenger of Vivasvat. May all others who are alike perish! 3

O Agni, for you, in your own mouth—that is, in your face—I offer these thoughts, which are worthy of reflection, just as others offer ghee that is pleasant like ghee itself; even so do I offer these hymns of praise.
As such, among the gods, recognize our praises; know them.
Moreover, you are the ancient one, the primordial.
You are Śiva and the bestower of happiness;
you are also the messenger of Vivasvat.
The rest is established.

Agni has assumed that vital power according as he acts with skillful art; an oblation of strength for the Vasus, he bestows well-being, security, and joy for every invocation of the gods. May all the others perish! He (Agni) has assumed that vigor, however much he exerts himself with skillful art. An offering of nourishment for the Vasus, he bestows well-being, security, and delight for every invocation of the gods. May all the others perish!
In whatever manner and whatever food the singers request from him, that very strength Agni bestows and grants to the singers.

Furthermore, being invoked with an oblation of vigor, Agni—himself the invoker—bestows and effects peace (*śam*) for the sake of the sacrificers who provide the offerings, as well as joy (*mayaḥ*), the happiness born from the attainment of objects, for their well-being.
He exists for every invocation of the gods and for the calling of all the deities.
The meaning is that if any deity whatsoever is invoked, it is Agni alone who accomplishes everything;
the rest is established.

He has taken notice through his most powerful, wondrous deed; he, the Hotṛ-priest of all the eternal ones, being sustained by sacrificial gifts, impels the offering toward the guest. May all others, the petty ones, be destroyed! He has taken notice with his most powerful, wondrous deed—that Agni. He, the Hotṛ-priest of all the eternal ones, being sustained by sacrificial gifts, impels the offering toward the guest. May all others, the petty ones, be destroyed! 5.
That Agni is known—that is, he is made manifest—by means of powerful, overwhelming, and manifold (citra) actions or activities.
That Agni, the invoker (hotṛ) of the many eternal deities, surrounded and encompassed by sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇās) and cattle, goes toward and strikes down the enemy who is to be encountered.
The rest is established.

Agni is the one born among the gods; Agni knows the secret of mortals. Agni is the giver of wealth; Agni, well-invoked with our newest hymn, throws open the doors. May all the others, the insignificant ones, perish! 6. Agni. Born. Of the gods. Agni. Knows. Of mortals. The secret. Agni. He. The giver of wealth. Agni. The doors. Apart. Throws open. Well-invoked. With the newest [hymn]. May they perish. The others. All. 6.
Agni knows the births and origins of the gods;
Agni knows the secret and hidden things of mortal men;
that Agni is the giver of wealth.
With a most recent oblation, well-sacrificed and properly offered, Agni opens wide the doors of wealth;
the rest is established.
Agni is the gatherer among the gods; he is among the clans worthy of sacrifice.
With joy, he, the god worthy of worship among the gods, nourishes many poetic insights throughout the whole earth as if with soil. May all others who are hostile perish!

Agni is the gatherer of wealth among the gods; he is among the clans worthy of sacrifice. He, the god worthy of worship among the gods, nourishes many poetic insights with joy, as a god nourishes the entire earth. May all others who are hostile perish! 7.
Among the gods, Agni dwells together with all things;
that Agni dwells together even among the *viktus*, the subjects worthy of sacrifice.
Moreover, that Agni nourishes many poetic works (*kāvya*) with joy, just as the earth nourishes everything with its delight.
Among the gods, Agni is the god who is worthy of sacrifice and fit for the ritual;
the rest is established.

That Agni who dwells among the seven human tribes, who is established in all the rivers—to him, the three-stepped Agni, the slayer of Dasyus, the holy one at sacrifices, we have come. May all others perish!
yo agniḥ saptamānuṣaḥ śrito viśveṣu sindhuṣu | tam āganma tripasyam mandhātur dasyuhantam agnim yajñeṣu puṇyam nabhantām anyake same ||

That Agni who dwells among the seven human tribes, who is established in all the rivers—to him we have come, to the one who watches over the three worlds, the most effective slayer of Dasyus for Mandhātṛ, the auspicious Agni at the sacrifices. May all others perish! || 8 ||

We have approached that Agni, who is the sevenfold friend of men, who is established in all the rivers, the three-seated (triple-stationed) son of Māndhātṛ—the son of Yuvanāśva—him who is the slayer of Dasyus, the preeminent one to be honored in the sacrifices.
The rest is self-evident.
Agni, the seer, dwells in the three [worlds] by means of his triple nature;
may he, the wise one, the messenger adorned as a priest, sacrifice here to the thrice eleven [gods] and satisfy them for us. May all others who are hostile perish!

Agni, the wise seer, dwells with his triple nature through his knowledge; may he, the inspired priest and appointed messenger, worship and satisfy the three times eleven gods here for us. May all others perish! 9.
The wise Agni, who beholds all that is beautiful, dwells in the three triple-layered abodes— the earth and the others— which are to be known as having three bonds and so forth;
moreover, that Agni, acting as the messenger of the gods, being a sage (*vipra*) and well-adorned, may he sacrifice here at this rite to the thirty-three gods—
the three sets of eleven— and may he satisfy us with our desires.
The rest is established.

1. *kha-gha-jña-ta1-2-veda* reads *veti*. 2. In *kha-ta-na-he*, it is *deveṣu*; in *ga-śa-yaḥ*, it is *deveṣu*. 3. In *kha-ga-ta-na-bha-śa*, it is *ā saṃvamuḥ*. 4. In *gha*, it is *saptamānuṣaḥ saptahotā*. 5. In *ta-na*, it is *mukhaṃ*.
O Agni, you alone rule over our lives and over the gods as the ancient lord of wealth.
The waters flow around you on all sides, like self-moving channels of the clouds. May all others who are hostile perish!
O Agni, you alone rule over wealth among us mortals and among the gods as the first; the waters that flow around you move in their own courses. May all others who are hostile perish! 10.

O ancient Agni, you alone among the Āyus— human beings, as indicated by the listing of *āyavaḥ* as a synonym for "men" (*manuṣya*) in the Nighaṇṭu— exercise sovereign power (*irajyasi*) over our wealth (*vasvaḥ*). You are the master of our riches.
Even among the gods, you alone, O Vasu, rule as sovereign.
Moreover, the *parisrut* waters—the flowing waters that constitute the very banks of their own channels—surround and flow around you.
The rest is self-evident.
The tenth hymn, consisting of twelve verses beginning with "indrāgnī yuvam," is the seerly composition of Nābhāka.
The second verse is a Śakvarī of fifty-six syllables, the twelfth is a Triṣṭubh, and the remaining verses are Mahāpaṅktis.
Indra and Agni are the deities.
And thus it has been listed in the Anukramaṇī: "The hymn beginning with 'indrāgnī' consists of twelve verses; it ends in Triṣṭubh, while the second verse is a Śakvarī.
This hymn belongs to the section on the thighs (*ūrubhāga*) in the Niṣkevalya of the Mahāvrata.
Accordingly, it is prescribed in the Pañcama Āraṇyaka: "'ūrū indrāgnī yuvaṃ su naḥ' (Ai. Ā. 5.3.1)."

If one should recite the *Mahāvratabhida* at the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*) on the twenty-fourth day during the *Maitrāvaruṇa* [sastra], then at the midday pressing (*mādhyandinasavana*), the Hotṛ priests should cause the *Nābhāka* verses to follow after the *Ārambhaṇīyā* verses in their respective *śastras*.
Among these, "tā hi madhyam" is the *Nābhāka* verse for the Acchāvāka.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "The Acchāvāka [recites] 'tā hi madhyaṃ bharaṇām'" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 7.2).
On the twenty-fourth day, at the midday pressing (*mādhyandinasavana*), the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin recites the *nābhāka* hymn beginning with "pūrvīr ta indra" (RV 10.89).
This is prescribed in the Sūtra: "The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin [recites] 'pūrvīr ta indropamātayaḥ'" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 7.2).

O Indra and Agni, you two who are victorious, grant us that wealth by which we may milk it out in battles and overcome even the firmest [foes] with our strength; let the others perish like forests before the wind in the conflict.

O Indra and Agni, you two, as conquerors, shall surely bestow wealth upon us, by which we may milk [the earth] and prevail even against the firm in battles. Like Agni or the wind consuming the forests, let all others who oppose us be struck down. 11.
O Indra and Agni, you two who are conquerors, overcoming the enemies—grant us, for our sake, wealth and riches abundantly.
He specifies that wealth:
by means of which wealth, even in battles, we may overcome even the most firm and solid enemy forces, just as the wind overcomes the forests; thus may we prevail and conquer.
The rest is established.
For we do not hold you back; rather, let us worship Indra, the most powerful hero among men.
May he come to us at any time with his steed for the winning of booty; may he come for the winning of booty. May all others perish in the conflict.

For we do not hold you two back; rather, we worship Indra alone, the most powerful hero among men. May he come to us at any time with his steed for the winning of booty; may he come for the winning of booty. Let all others perish utterly! 12.
1. *ta1-2-svasetava* | 2. *jñāta-su* means "well" (*suṣṭhu*). 3. *gata-na-bha-‘datta’* means "there is not. 4. *bha3-saṃgrāmeṣu*.
O Indra and Agni, we do not beg you two for wealth as if it were our own.
Rather, indeed, we worship only Indra—the most powerful, the preeminent leader among men, the leader even of leaders.
May that Indra come to us with his steed, at any time, for the winning of booty—that is, for the acquisition of food;
may he come at any time for the winning of the sacrifice—that is, for the distribution of the sacrificial portion.
The rest is self-evident.

For those two, Indra and Agni, dwell in the midst of the battles; they indeed, O doers, being questioned through their poetic wisdom, have fully heard the unheeded prayer for the sake of the one who desires friendship. O heroes, let them strike down the enemies in the encounter. Those two—the well-known Indra and Agni—dwell in the midst of the battles (bharāṇām), that is, they preside over them. Now follows the direct praise: O leaders (narā), O doers (kavī) of wondrous deeds through your poetic wisdom (kavitvanā), you two, being questioned by the wise, have fully heard (saṃ aśrutam) the prayer (dhītam)—the work performed—for the sacrificer who desires friendship (sakhīyate). The rest is established.

Worship Indra and Agni with sacrifice and song, as Nabhaka did—those two by whose lap this entire world, this heaven, and this great earth abide; they, the all-pervading ones, bestow wealth upon us. May our enemies perish in the conflict. O Nabhaka, worship Indra and Agni with sacrifice and with song—those two by whose lap this entire world stands, and in whose lap both this heaven and the great earth hold their wealth. The rest is established.

Let the sacred hymns be directed forth toward Indra and Agni, as Nābhāka did. They two who unrolled the ocean with seven springs, whose gate was the tongue—Indra, the sovereign by his might, is the lord over them; let the others perish in the conflict. The sacred hymns (*brahmāṇi*) are the songs of praise. Let them be directed forth toward Indra and Agni, as Nābhāka did. Those two, Indra and Agni, who unrolled the ocean—which had seven springs, whose gate was hidden by the tongue, and which was covered by their splendors—between those two, Indra is the sovereign by his power. The rest is established. 1. *gha-ta-na-bha-pṛcchyamānau* | 2. *ta-na-bha-'yā' nāsti* |
Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 40. The Sixth Aṣṭaka. 735.

And furthermore, O Bull (Indra), like one of old, with your vows, as it were—cut down the power that has been gathered, like a branch that has sprouted forth. Strike down the strength of the Dāsa, the enemy named Dāsa! May we, through Indra, divide among ourselves that wealth accumulated by him. Let the others perish in the conflict! And furthermore: O Indra, like one of ancient times, with your sacred observances (*vrata*), as if with axes, cut down the power that has been gathered, just as one cuts a branch that has emerged. He says this very thing: strike down—that is, destroy—the strength (*ojaḥ*) of the Dāsa, the enemy named Dāsa. Now follows the praise in the third person: we, the Nābhākas, through Indra as our means, shall divide among ourselves the wealth accumulated by this Dāsa. The rest is established. 24.
O Indra and Agni, since these people invoke you with various songs, may we, through our own hymns, overcome those who attack us and conquer those who seek to conquer us, O heroes!

O you two of golden-hued steeds, O wielder of the thunderbolt, O Son of Power, O impeller, send forth wealth for the one who delights in it; bestow the riches of the hero who gathers them. These are your peerless deeds—your many and ancient exploits.
And furthermore, those many praises which have perfected— that is, brought to fulfillment—
our prayers and our wisdom;
the rest is established.
Sharpen him with well-fashioned hymns—he who is the impetuous one among beings, beyond measure.
And he indeed, by his might, shatters the eggs of Śuṣṇa; he wins the waters together with the sun. May all others, every one of them, be destroyed!

Sharpen him with well-fashioned hymns—he who is the brilliant, powerful, and impetuous one; he who indeed by his might shatters the eggs of Śuṣṇa. May he cause the waters to flow forth with the sun; may all others perish utterly! 10.
O singers, sharpen—that is, prepare with praise—Indra, the radiant one, the bestower of wealth upon living beings, the one to be extolled with *ṛc* verses, by means of well-fashioned hymns.
And furthermore, may that Indra, who by his might (*ojas*) shattered the eggs—the egg-born offspring—of the Asura named Śuṣṇa, conquer the heavenly waters, the celestial floods.
The rest is established.
Sharpen that true, immortal sovereign of beings;
even now, those who are his destroyers shall shatter the eggs of Śuṣṇa. O you who possess the sun, let all the others, every one of them, perish!

Sharpen him—the true one among beings, the seer who makes the sacrifice well-performed; and indeed, he who boasts, let him shatter the eggs of Śuṣṇa. With his goats, may he win the waters rich in sunlight. Let all others, the insignificant ones, perish! 11.

O singers, sharpen—that is, prepare with praises—that Indra who possesses a good sacrifice, who is true, who destroys his enemies, who is the bestower of strength, who is worthy of praise, and who is to be worshipped at the proper season. Now follows a direct praise:

Moreover, that very Indra who goes toward the sacrifice and shatters—the word *bhedati* being from *bhid*, "to split"—the eggs and egg-born offspring of Śuṣṇa; you, such as he are, have won the heavenly waters, the celestial floods, together with the sun.
The rest is established.
Thus, for Indra and Agni, a newer [hymn] has been spoken, like that of the fathers, like that of Māndhātṛ, and like that of Aṅgiras.
With your triple-layered protection, protect us; may we be masters of riches.
Thus, O Indra and Agni, like fathers, more recently, like Māndhātṛ, like Aṅgiras, it has been spoken. With a triple-layered protection, guard us. May we be masters of riches. 12.

Just so, to those two, Indra and Agni, for whom [this hymn] has been recited by me, Nābhāka, more newly—just as it was for Pitṛvat, Nabhakavat, Mandhātṛvat (the son of Yuvanāśva), and Aṅgirasvat—may Indra and Agni, through their threefold, three-jointed protection and shelter, protect us, the Nābhākas;
and may we become masters and lords of riches.
1. In the *ga*, *ta*, *na*, and *bha* [recensions], "of the son" (*sūnoḥ*) does not exist.
2. In the *ta*, *na*, *bha*, and *ra* [recensions], it is either "wealth" (*vasvaḥ*).
3. In the *kha*, *ga*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, and *śa* [recensions], "he splits, he cleaves" (*bhedati bhinatti*) does not exist; in the *gha* [recension], it is "he split" (*abhinat*).

4. In the *ga-gṛha* there are no *asmājñāḥ*; in the *ta-na-bha-gṛha* there are no *asmājñāḥ*. The eleventh hymn consists of ten verses beginning with “asmā ū ṣu. Regarding this, the *Aṅkramaṇikā* states: “asmā ū ṣu daśa vāruṇaṃ tu” (the ten [verses] beginning with asmā ū ṣu are addressed to Varuṇa).

Nābhāka is a seer because of his composition in the *anuṣṭubh* meter; for it has been stated that "he is indeed a great seer" (*mahārṣi*), he is therefore also a great seer (*mahārṣi*). These two initial hymns have Varuṇa as their deity.
The application is indicated by the context.

On the twenty-fourth day, during the midday pressing (*mādhyandina-savana*), in the *maitrāvaruṇa-śastra*, following the *ārambhaṇīyā* verse, there is this *nābhāka* hymn beginning with "sa kṣapaḥ. And it is stated in the Sūtra: "The *maitrāvaruṇa* [recites] 'sa kṣapaḥ pari ṣasvaje' and so forth" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 7.2).
Or else, this [verse] beginning with “yaḥ kakubhaḥ” belongs to Nābhāka;
for it is stated in the Sūtra: “‘yaḥ kakubho nidhāraya’ or [the verse beginning with] ‘yaḥ kakubhaḥ’” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 7.2).
Sing forth for his great assistance— for Varuṇa and the Maruts, who are most wise—
he who protects the thoughts of men like cattle, and strikes down the enemies in battle.

Sing for him—*ūm*!—for the sake of great abundance, for Varuṇa, and for the Maruts, who are most wise. He who, like a herdsman guarding his cattle, protects the thoughts of men; let all others perish in my assembly. 1.
O singer, praise this Varuṇa for his abundant prosperity, and sing hymns to the Maruts, who are most wise.
That Varuṇa, through his wisdom and action, protects the cattle of men like [a herdsman protects] cows. (The rest is the same as before.)
Him indeed with a common song and with the hymns of the fathers,
with the praises of Nābhāka— at the rising of the rivers, he, the middle one among the seven sisters, is the slayer of the enemy in the encounter.

Him, indeed, with the word "Ūm," with a well-ordered song, and with the prayers of the fathers, and with the praises of Nābhāka—him who, at the rising of the rivers, is accompanied by the seven sisters; may he, the center of men, destroy the others in the encounter. 2.
I praise him alone, O Varuṇa, with every equal song—that is, with uniform hymns of praise;
I praise him with the prayers of the fathers;
and I praise him with the eulogies and chants of the seer Nābhāka.

He who rises near the flowing rivers—that is, the streams—and who is called "the Middle One" by words such as "he who has seven sisters"—may all those other evil-minded enemies perish together; let them not exist. Thus says Yāska: "I praise him with a unified song, having sung with hymns worthy of the ancestors and with the praises of Nābhāka."
"He became the portion of the seers;
he who, at the rising of these [waters] as they flow, addressed this seven-sistered one with words, is defined as 'the Middle One' (madhyama); and he indeed becomes thus:
'May others not be near me; may all those who hate us—evil-minded, wicked-minded, and evil-intentioned—be far away'" (Nirukta 10.5).
He has embraced the night; by his creative power he has established the dawn. He is visible all around the universe.
His two beloved wives have indeed increased his rite—the three [worlds]—while the others remain small within me.

He has embraced the nights; by his creative power he has established them. He is visible all around the universe. Following his law, the longing ones have caused the three worlds to grow. May the others be subject to our control.

1. *kha* as *ta*; *ga* as *ca*; *na* and *bha* as *iva*; *śa* as [itself]. 2. *ga*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, and *ra*: *gacchati* (goes) as if he protects (*rakṣati*); *gha* means "he protects" just as a cowherd protects his cows; *bha* means "he goes. (Ka. 1.47)
Varuṇa embraces the nights; he wraps himself around them.

Moreover, that beautiful Varuṇa, being ever-advancing, places everything all around by means of his creative power (*māyā*) and his work. Furthermore, the three dawns—the people who desire his sacred law (*vrata*)—increase it throughout the three times: morning, midday, and evening.
The rest is established.
He who has fixed the two ridges of the earth, visible below;
he is the measurer of that ancient station, the sevenfold path of Ṛguṇa, for he is the guardian of the herd. May the others perish in their conflict!

He who has firmly established the quarters upon the earth, he who is beautiful to behold—he is the measurer of the ancient station; that is the sevenfold domain of Varuṇa. For he is like a watchful guardian. Let all others perish in the conflict! 4.

Varuṇa, who is visible upon the earth and even above the earth, being beautiful to behold, supports the quarters—the cardinal directions—from their foundations; that Varuṇa is the fashioner and the creator. That ancient, primordial station known as heaven, the seventh place to be traversed by us—that is the self-made abode of Varuṇa. Moreover, he alone, being the powerful Lord, is our protector like a shepherd protecting his cattle.
The rest is established.
He who is the upholder of the worlds, who knows the secret names of those born from the source—he, the seer, nourishes many poetic forms like the sky; may our enemies perish in the conflict!

He who is the upholder of the worlds, who knows the secret, hidden names of the creatures—he, the seer, fosters many poetic insights in manifold forms, like the sky; let all others perish in my contest! 5.

Varuṇa, the upholder of the worlds, who knows the secret, hidden, and mysterious names of the rays that have been emitted and which serve as the divine foundations—he, Varuṇa, being a wise seer (*kavi*), as a sage nourishes many poetic works (*kāvyā*) like the sky nourishes forms.
The rest is established.

In whom all poetic insights are centered as if in a nave—worship Trita with fervor! Like cows in a stall, they have harnessed their horses for the yoking; may those who hold other views be destroyed in our conflict.

In whom all poetic insights are centered as if upon a nave—honor Trita with fervor! Like cattle gathered in a pen, they have harnessed their horses for the union. May all others perish in the encounter! 6.

In this Varuṇa all (viśvāni) poetic works (kāvyā)—the deeds of a seer—are fixed, just as the nave is fixed in the wheel of a chariot. Worship (saparyata) with speed (jūtī) that Varuṇa, the threefold one (tritam), who has three stations; O my people, serve him! For what purpose? He says: so that the cows may be joined together in the pen (vraje) for the sake of union, like cattle in a cow-pen.
They have yoked the horses.
May they perish!
To others!
To the assembly!
1. Kha-ta-ma: svanuta; ga: svahata; na: tutaṃ; bha-śa: svabhūtaṃ. 2. Ta-na-bha: arthaḥ. 3. Gha: tritaṃ bhūrbhuvaḥsvaḥ.
I have harnessed [the chariot] to stand together; likewise, they have yoked the horses for our exertion. They yoke them along with the enemy.
Therefore, the meaning is: O Varuṇa, attend to him in order to avoid that affliction—[he] who dwells among these, [and] all their births.
Touching all the abodes of Varuṇa, he lies around them like a garment; he surveys all their births and their stations for the sake of our household. May all the gods follow his decree!
May those others perish, yea, may they utterly vanish!

He who lies around these as a garment, surveying all their births and their stations for the sake of our household—may all the gods follow his decree! May those others perish, yea, may they utterly vanish!
As he touches [the reins], Varuṇa stands before the house, that is, in front of the chariot; all the gods follow his ordinance—that is the meaning.
The rest is established.
He, the hidden ocean, rises up like the swift heaven when he has placed the sacrificial formula within these [waters].
He who spread out the earth with his foot by means of illusion;

he who made the white ones subject to himself and the black ones subject to Arjuna; he measured out the ancient abode; he, the Unborn, supported heaven with a pillar as if it were the two worlds, Rodasī; let all others be subdued. 10.

Varuṇa spreads out his own rays, white by day and black at night; thus Varuṇa, according to his ordinances—the various deeds corresponding to the two kinds of actions characterized by light—measured out the ancient abode, whether the intermediate space or heaven. Moreover, as the Sun (Āditya), like an unaging one, sustains the sky through the pillar that is the intermediate space, so Varuṇa has established and maintains the two worlds, heaven and earth.
The rest is self-evident.

The twelfth hymn, consisting of six verses beginning with "astabhnāt," has Arcanānas Kāṇva as its seer, or alternatively, Nābhāka as the seer; however, the two subsequent verses have Nābhāka as the seer.
The first triplet is in the *triṣṭubh* meter and has Varuṇa as its deity; the second triplet is in the *anuṣṭubh* meter and has the Aśvins as its deities.
Thus it is stated in the *Anukramaṇī*: "He supported [the earth]; there are six verses, either two separate *triṣṭubh*s or a *triṣṭubh* and an *anuṣṭubh* triplet; he saw [this] Aśvin hymn.
The application (*viniyoga*) of this hymn is based on its internal characteristics (*laiṅgika*).
The invitatory verse for the oblation at the Vāruṇa animal sacrifice is “He has propped up” (*astabhnāt*).
And it is stated in the Sūtra: “‘He, the Asura, the all-knowing, propped up the earth’—these are the eleven [verses]” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.7).
In the *agnīṣomapraṇayana* as well, this same verse is the concluding *paridhānīyā*.
Thus it is stated in the Sūtra: “One should conclude with ‘He, the all-knowing Asura, has propped up the sky,’ or with the next [verse]” (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 4.10).
“‘Thus praise Varuṇa the Great; I approach you, praising with a prayer’—these two [verses]” (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 3.7).
In the *Somapravahaṇa* [rite], the verse beginning with "imāṃ dhiyam" is the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*).
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "At the conclusion of the rite, one should recite 'imāṃ dhiyaṃ śikṣamāṇasya deva' as the concluding verse" (*Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra* 4.4).

The Asura, the knower of all, propped up the sky; he measured out the expanse of the earth. As sovereign lord, he took his seat over all worlds—all these indeed are the ordinances of Varuṇa. He propped up the sky; the Asura, the possessor of all knowledge, measured out the breadth of the earth. He, the sovereign ruler, has taken his seat over all worlds. All these indeed are the sacred laws of Varuṇa.

Varuṇa, the all-knowing, the possessor of all wealth, the powerful Asura, propped up the sky; likewise, he measured out the vast extent of the earth. Having become the sovereign ruler, he has taken his seat and presides over all these created worlds.
These very deeds (vratāni) of Varuṇa are ordained as all-encompassing;
that is to say, they are impossible to fully describe. 4.

Thus worship Varuṇa, the lofty one; pay homage to the wise guardian of immortality. May he grant us a triple-layered shelter; may Heaven and Earth protect us in their lap. 2. Thus. Worship. Varuṇa. The lofty one. Pay homage. To the wise. Guardian of immortality. He. Us. Shelter. Triple-layered. May he bestow. Protect. Us. Heaven-and-Earth. In their lap. 2.
O singer, praise and extol Varuṇa in this very way—the great and vast one;
the protector of immortality, the wise and discerning one—pay homage to Varuṇa.
May that Varuṇa grant us a triple-sheltered [protection] with three stations, whose back is directed toward all the gods.
2. In manuscript Gha, there is [the word] "of such a Varuṇa.
3. In manuscripts Ta, Na, and Bha, the word "vratāni" (vows) is absent.
4. In manuscript Gha, it says "there are many."

May [Heaven and Earth] extend wide shelter; may they grant us a home. O Heaven and Earth, you who dwell in the lap of the lap, protect us. O God Varuṇa, sharpen this prayer of the one practicing it, sharpen his insight and his skill. By which we may cross over all difficulties, may we ascend the ship that carries us well across. O God, O radiant Varuṇa, sharpen this prayer of mine as I practice it; sharpen my insight and my strength. By means of that [ship]—which is the sacrifice—may we cross over all misfortunes; may we ascend that ship which carries us well across. Because it is the cause for crossing the ocean of suffering, the sacrifice is designated here as a "ship. The pressing-stones, O Aśvins, have been raised up for you by the wise with their prayers. O Nāsatyas, come for the drinking of the Soma; let the others cease in the assembly. O Nāsatyas, truthful ones, leaders of truth—so says Yāska: "Nāsatyas are indeed the two Truthful Ones, the leaders of truth" (Nirukta 6.13)—O Aśvins, for the drinking of the Soma, the wise priests and the pressing-stones have raised you up with their prayers through their respective duties. The rest is established. Just as the wise Atri called upon you both, O Aśvins, with songs for the drinking of the Soma, O Nāsatyas, so do I call upon you. Thus have the wise called upon you for our protection, O Nāsatyas, for the drinking of the Soma; let the others cease in the assembly. This verse has already been explained. 28. 5.
1. *Jha-bha-nāsatyau*.
In the sixth section (*anuvāka*), there are six hymns (*sūkta*).

Among them, the first hymn, consisting of thirty-three verses beginning with "These [songs] of the sage" (*ime viprasya*), is the seerage of Virūpa Āṅgirasa; it is in the *gāyatrī* meter and has Agni as its deity.
And thus it has been listed in the Anukramaṇī: "These thirty-three [verses] belong to Virūpa Āṅgirasa; however, they are addressed to Agni.
These two hymns beginning with this one are used in the Prātaranuvāka during the Āgneya sacrifice, in the Gāyatrī metre, and for the Aśvina-śastra.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "'These [are] of the sage,' these two hymns" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.13).

For the first butter-portion (*ājyabhāga*) of the cow at the *avabhṛtha* sacrifice of the *kārīrī*, the invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) is "In the waters" (*apsv antaḥ*). Thus it is stated in the Sūtra: "The two butter-portions contain the word 'water': 'In the waters,' 'Upon your seat'" (*āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 2.13). It is also the *prasthitayājyā* for the Āgnīdhra at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*).
And it is heard [in scripture]: "The Āgnīdhra priest sacrifices with the [mantras] 'For the bull-eater,' 'For the cow-eater'" (AiB 6.10).
In the Agnivati sacrifice, "tvam hyagne" is the *yājyā*.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "'tvam hyagne agninā tvam astu yudhām amīvāḥ'" (ĀśvŚS 3.13).

In the sacrifice with the *agnimanyu* [offering], it is stated in the Sūtra: "O Agni, you indeed [are purified] by Agni; they cleanse him who performs good deeds" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 2.16). In the eight-potsherd sacrifice for Agni Kāma, the verse "To you, O best of the Aṅgirases" is the invitatory verse (*anu-vākyā*).

And it is stated in the Sūtra: "We offer these to you, O best of the Aṅgiras; fulfill that desire, O Agni, through your protection"—this is for the sake of a specific desire (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 2.10).
When one who has maintained the sacred fires sets out on a journey, if he chooses the method of re-depositing the fires, this single oblation must be performed.
Accordingly, the Sūtra states: "Having offered a clarified-butter oblation with the verse 'To you, O best of the Aṅgiras,' he should perform the re-deposit" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 3.10).
In the case of a combination of Vaiśvānara, Agni, and Prāpti offerings, there is an offering to Agni Apsumat.
In that rite, the *yājyā* verse is "O Agni, those born in heaven...
and "O Agni, those born in heaven, he who sat down here as the most excellent invoker" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 3.13).
These songs and hymns of the inspired sage, the wise Agni, the invincible sacrificer, go forth. 1. These songs and hymns of the inspired sage, the wise Agni, the invincible sacrificer, go forth. 1.
These hymns of ours—the praises of the wise, inspired, and ordaining priest who performs unimpeded sacrifice, and the songs of the unharmed sacrificer—urge forth the laudations of Agni.

For you, O Jātavedas, who take delight in this [offering], O Agni, observer of men, I generate a beautiful hymn of praise. 2. For you; for you; taking delight; O Jātavedas; O observer of men; O Agni; I generate; a beautiful hymn of praise. 2.

O Jātavedas, whose wealth is born, O Agni, you who shine far and wide and see all things—O Agni, for you who take pleasure in this [offering] and bestow it, I, an Aṅgiras, produce for you a beautiful hymn of praise; I generate it.

Like rays of light, indeed, O Agni, are your sharp flashes; with them you devour the forests as they run. 3. Like rays of light—verily, indeed—O Agni, your sharp flashes; with them, running, you devour the forests. 3.
O Agni, your sharp and keen splendors, shining like rays of light, devour the forests and wild woods with their teeth as if they were beasts;
"ghedaha" is an expletive used for filling out the verse.

The bay-colored ones, whose banner is smoke, impelled by the wind, strive individually toward the sky—the fires. 4. The bay-colored ones; whose banner is smoke; impelled by the wind; toward; the sky; strive; individually; the fires. 4.

The *harayaḥ*—those whose nature is to carry away, impelled by the wind, driven by the wind, smoke-bannered fires—strive and move separately, individually, toward the sky, that is, in the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*). By this [use of] "separately" (*pṛthak*), it is understood as "equally" (*samam*) or "simultaneously" (*abhiyugapad*).
Indeed, the Vājasaneyins recite simply "separately" (*pṛthak*) [in the text]: *pṛthag u yad ajagantoro-mātrāṃ divedive* (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā 33.2).
These various fires, once kindled, have flared up together like the banners of the dawns.

1. *ga-jha-taya-* ‘separately’ does not exist; *tara-3-bha-* ‘separately’. These, those—these immortals, shining brightly, have appeared together like the banners of the dawns. || 5 || These, those—these immortals, shining brightly, having been kindled separately by the *abhihotṛ* priests, have appeared together like the banners of the dawns, that is, like the indicators of the dawns; they are clearly seen. || 29 ||

The dust from the feet of Jātavedas becomes black upon his departure, when Agni spreads across the earth. The dust from the feet of Jātavedas becomes black upon his departure, when Agni spreads across the earth. When? It is said: when Agni spreads across the earth—that is, when he obstructs the dry trees.

Making the plants his nourishment, Agni, devouring them, does not grow weary; he goes again even unto the young ones. Making the plants his nourishment—*dhāsi* being read among the names for food in the list beginning with *śruta dhāsi*—Agni, while making [them] his and devouring them, does not grow weary (*na vāyati*). Furthermore, he goes (*yan*) even unto the young plants; the ellipsis is "in order to devour."

With his tongues, indeed, bending the forest trees, he became manifest with his flame; Agni shines among the woods. (8) With his tongues—that is, with his very flames—he, indeed, bending the lords of the forest (the trees) completely, became manifest with his radiance—that is, he blazed forth. This is because the root *jajñaṇābhavat* is listed among the verbs meaning "to blaze. He shines, that is, he illuminates, among the woods, that is, in the forests.

O Agni, your dwelling is in the waters; you grow forth following the plants. Being in their womb, you are born again. (9) O Agni, you whose dwelling (*sadhiḥ*)—that is, your place of entry—is in the waters (*apsu*), you, being such, grow forth (*rudhyase*) following (*anu*) the plants (*oṣadhīḥ*). And again, being in their womb (*garbhe san*) while they are situated upon the earth, you are born (*jāyase*), that is, you manifest yourself. (9)

O Agni, that flame of yours shines forth from the clarified butter when offered, licking at the mouth of the sacrificial ladle. 10 O Agni, that flame of yours shines forth from the clarified butter when offered, licking at the mouth of the sacrificial ladle—the instrument of oblation. 10 O Agni, that flame of yours, licking—that which licks—the clarified butter offered at the mouth of the *juhū* (the ladle used as the means of oblation), shines forth; it is radiant. 10.30.

To the bull, to the one who has the cow as his food, whose back is laden with Soma, the ordainer—to Agni, let us do service with hymns of praise. 11. To the bull-eater; to the cow-eater; to the one whose back is Soma; to the ordainer; with hymns; let us do service; to Agni. 11.

1. Ga, gha, ta, na, and bha were distinct. 2. Kha, gha, jña, and the second ta were black; they were all black. 3. Ga, tara, ra, and massanā did not come into being; jña and bhassanā did not come into being; na and manānā did not come into being.
4. There is no *niśāna* for *ga*, *ta*, *na*.
5. [The substitution of] *kha*, *na*, *gha*, *ta*, *na*, *jña*, *ni*, *li*, *hā* occurs after *vu*, *kṣā*, and *nnā*.
He for whom the exhilarating oblation is the bull is "Ukṣan";
to him, who has the cow as his desire, [is addressed] "Vaśānna"; he for whom the cow is his desire is "Vaśā."
To him whose back is Soma, whose back is ghee, to the Ordainer, the Disposer of desires—to Agni, we offer worship with our hymn of praise.

And so, O Hotṛ of most excellent wisdom, we, the Aṅgirases, approach you with reverence, O Agni, and with kindled fuel. (12) And furthermore, O Hotṛ—invoker of the gods—O Agni of desirable wisdom, we [the Aṅgirases] approach you with homage, with oblations, and with fuel-sticks. We entreat you.

And we invoke you, O pure one, as Bhrigu did, as Manu did, O Agni, you who are invoked with oblations, as Angiras did. (13) O pure one, naturally stainless; O Agni, you who are invoked with oblations—we invoke you just as Bhrigu did, just as Manu did, and just as Angiras did.

For you, O Agni, being a sage (*vipra*) and existing as a friend, are kindled by a sage and by a friend through [the fire] itself. O Agni, you who are a sage (*vipra*), being present (*san*) and a friend (*sakhā*), are kindled (*samidhyase*) by a sage (*vipreṇa*) and by a friend (*sakhyā*) through the fire (*agninā*). Thus says the Brāhmaṇa: "For you, O Agni, being a sage by a sage, existing by that which exists... a friend by a friend is kindled; this indeed is his own friend" (AiB 1.16).

As such, O Agni, grant to the wise donor who has offered oblations wealth consisting of thousands, and food accompanied by heroic sons. 15. O Agni, you who are renowned, grant to the wise one—the sacrificer who has given offerings—wealth measured by the thousands, and food accompanied by heroes, such as sons and grandsons. 13.

O Agni, brother, created by strength, with ruddy horses, of pure vows—be pleased with this hymn of mine. (16) "O Agni, brother," "created by strength," "with ruddy horses," "of pure vows"—"this hymn," "be pleased with," "mine. (16) O Agni, brother—acting as a friend to the sacrificers like a brother; O you who were created by strength, i.e., by power; O you whose horses are ruddy-colored; O you of pure vows, i.e., of purified actions—O Agni, be pleased with, i.e., accept, this hymn of mine, [I,] the descendant of Aṅgiras.

And indeed, O Agni, praised by me, you have reached [the sacrifice] like lowing cows reaching the cow-pen for their lowing calf that longs for the path. And indeed, O Agni, praised by me, you have reached [the sacrifice] like lowing cows reaching the cow-pen—just as cows enter the pen for their lowing calf that longs for the path, desiring to drink milk. You, being praised by me, the descendant of Aṅgiras, have reached [the sacrifice] for the lowing calf that longs for the path, desiring to milk it. Just as cows enter the cow-pen, so have they reached you with their lowing.
1. Gha: "And also, O"; 2. Gha: "by the virtuous one"; 3. Kha, Ga, Ta, Na, Bha, Śa: "accompanied by"; 4. Jha, Ta, La, E: "of me, mine."

To you, O best of the Aṅgirases, all those well-settled people have separately submitted for the sake of their desire, O Agni. (18) O best of the Aṅgirases, O Agni, to you—those well-settled people, all of them, have each individually submitted for the sake of their own desire, that is, for the fulfillment of their wishes. (18)

The wise, the intelligent, and the learned, through their mental powers, urge Agni forward for the sake of attaining his limbs. (19) The wise—those who are masters of the mind, the intelligent, the learned, and the sagacious—through their *dhīs* (mental powers or ritual acts), urge Agni forward for the sake of attaining his limbs (*aṅgasadhāya*), that is, for the purpose of partaking in his limbs. They propitiate him.

O Agni, those who extend the sacrifice among the goat-sacrificers praise you—the renowned one—as the powerful bearer, the carrier of oblations, and the invoker of the gods. 20. O Agni, those performing the sacrifice among the goat-sacrificers—extending the *adhvara* (sacrifice)—praise you, the well-known one, as the powerful (*vājin*) bearer (*vahni*), the carrier of offerings, and the invoker (*hotṛ*) of the deities. 20. O Agni, the sacrificers, extending the *adhvara* (sacrifice) among the goat-sacrificers—that is, in their homes—praise you, the famous one, as the powerful, the bearer of oblations, and the invoker of the gods. 32.

For in many places you are the one who looks upon all; you are the lord over all the clans. In battles we invoke you. (21) For in many places, O Agni, you are indeed the one who looks upon [all] equally (*saha-dṛś*); by a Vedic elision [of *d*], you are the lord (*prabhu*) over all the clans (*viśaḥ*), that is, over all the subjects (*prajāḥ*). Therefore, in battles (*samatsu*), we invoke you. (21)

Praise that Agni who, when invoked with offerings of clarified butter, shines forth brilliantly; may he hear this our invocation. (22) Praise him—Agni—who, being invoked with offerings of clarified butter, shines forth intensely; and may he hear, indeed, this our call. Praise that Agni. (22) That Agni who, when offered oblations along with clarified butter, blazes brightly, and who hears—listens to—this our invocation, his call: praise that Agni. (22)

We invoke you, O Agni, the Jātavedas who hears us, who strikes away our enemies. 23 We, the Aṅgirases, invoke you—O Agni, the Jātavedas (knower of all beings), who possesses innate wealth or innate wisdom—who strikes away our enemies, who slays them, and who hears our invocation. 23

I praise this Agni, the wonderful king of the people, the overseer of the sacred laws; may he indeed hear me. 24. Of the people, the king, the wonderful, the overseer, of the sacred laws, this—Agni—I praise; he, verily, shall hear. 24.
1. *gha-ta-na-bha-ra-ya-prajñā*:
2. *ta-na-bha*—the word "hotāram" (priest) is not present.

He who is the *rājānam* (king), the lord of *viśām* (the people/subjects), the *amṛtam* (immortal), the *mahāntam* (great), the *adhyakṣam* (overseer) and *anusaṃdhātāram* (director) of *dharmaṇām* (deeds/actions)—him, whom I here praise (*abhimīḷe*), that very Agni (*sa u sa evāgniḥ*) shall hear (*śravat*) our hymn of praise.
We incite Agni, who stirs all life, like a prize-winning steed set forth in the contest for men, as we urge on a swift horse. 25.
We stir Agni, who possesses all-encompassing vitality, like a prize-winning mortal steed set to the race, as we urge on a chariot-horse with our speed. ||25||

We strengthen with hymns and oblations Agni, who possesses all-encompassing power and universal strength—the powerful one, like a mortal man, the well-disposed one, and like a courser; we make him strong.
O Agni, slaying the fierce ones, driving away our enemies, and burning up the demons forever, shine forth with your sharp flame! 26.
Slaying the obstructors, driving away our enemies, and burning up the demons at all times, O Agni, shine forth with your sharp flame! 26.
O Agni, do thou indeed strike away the harmful ones, the enemies who hate us; destroying them and burning up the Rākṣasas at all times, shine forth with thy sharp and piercing splendor!
O Agni, best of the Aṅgirases, whom men kindle like Manu, be thou my luster! 27.
O Agni, best of the Angirases, you whom the people kindle like Manu—be mindful of my splendor. 27.
O Agni, best of the Aṅgirases, you whom the people kindle like Manu—do thou, being thus kindled, take note of my speech, that is, my hymn of praise.
O Agni, whether thou art born from heaven or born from the waters, O thou who art strengthened by force, we invoke thee with our songs. 28.
O Agni, whether you are born in heaven or born in the waters, O you who are made of strength, we invoke you with our songs. 28.

O Agni, since you are born in heaven, dwelling in the sky, or since you are born in the waters, arisen in the intermediate space, and since you are made by strength—that is, produced by power—we invoke you, that very Agni, with our songs of praise.
For you indeed, all these people, these various well-settled communities, separately send forth nourishment for the sake of the sacred order (ṛta). 29.
Truly, these people—all these well-settled communities—send forth nourishment for you individually, according to the cosmic order.

O Agni, for you alone—indeed, for your sake—these people whom I see, and all these well-settled subjects, separately impel and urge forth the nourishment, the oblation, for you to eat. O Agni, may we, being well-disposed toward you and watching over men, pass through all the days and cross over all difficulties. 30.
O Agni, may we—being well-disposed toward you, worthy, and beholders of men—cross over all difficulties. 30.

O Agni, for your sake alone, being well-studious (*svādhyas*) and performing good deeds (*sukarmāṇas*), may we, as beholders of men (*nṛcakṣasas*), cross over all days (*viśvā ahā*) and traverse the difficult-to-traverse paths (*durgāhā*). 34.1. (Note variants: *abhimīḷe*; "dīpyasva" is absent; *hayāma*; *ghet*.)

We implore Agni with heart-pleasing and delightful hymns—the one who is charming, beloved by many, fierce, and possessed of purifying luster. (31) We implore Agni—the charming, the much-beloved, the fierce, whose radiance is purifying—with hearts that are delightful and pleasing. (31) We implore Agni—who is charming (meaning exhilarating), beloved by many, fierce (lying in wait at sacrifices), and possessing purifying brilliance—with heart-captivating, delightful, and exhilarating hymns; we entreat him.

O Agni, you who possess radiant wealth, like the sun rising and emitting its rays, you, being powerful, destroy the darkness. 32. O Agni, you who possess radiant wealth (vibhāvasu), that well-known you, like the sun—just as the sun—emitting [light] and being powerful, exerting strength with your rays, you destroy the darkness; you annihilate it.
Therefore, O powerful one, we implore you for this gift.

O Agni, enjoy my hymn of praise; grow strong by this thought; graciously accept our well-spoken words. (2) I place Agni at the forefront as the messenger; I address him, the bearer of oblations, that he may seat the gods here. (3) The great flames of thee, O shining Agni, being kindled, rise upward—thy pure, radiant rays. (4) Let the ladles dripping with clarified butter approach thee, O beloved one; O Agni, graciously accept our offerings. (5) I praise Agni—the delightful invoker, the seasonal priest, of wondrous luster and radiant wealth; may he indeed hear us. (6) I praise Agni—the ancient invoker, worthy of praise, beloved, of wise intellect, the glory of the sacrifices. (7) O Agni, best of the Angirases, enjoying these offerings in succession, lead the sacrifice according to the seasons. (8)

O worthy one, O you of pure luster, being kindled, bring here, as one who knows, the divine folk. 9. O worthy one (*santya*), you who are disposed to receive offerings, O you of pure luster (*śukraśoce*), while being kindled (*samidhānaḥ*), knowing (*cikittvān*) the divine folk (*daivyam janam*)—those connected with the gods—bring them here (*iha*) to this sacrifice. 9.

We pray to the wise one, the invoker, the guileless, whose banner is smoke, the source of light, the signal of sacrifices. (10) To the *vipra*—the inspired sage; the *hotṛ*—the invoker of the gods; the *adruhaḥ*—the one free from deceit; the *dhūmaketum*—whose banner is smoke; the *vibhāvasum*—the possessor of radiant splendor; the *ketum yajñānām*—the ensign or standard of sacrifices; we *īmahe*—we entreat him for our desired goal. (10) The *vipra* is the wise one; the *hotṛ* is the caller of the gods; the *adruhaḥ* is the one without malice; the *dhūmaketum* is he whose banner is smoke; the *vibhāvasum* is the one whose wealth is light; the *ketum yajñānām* is Agni, who stands in the place of a banner or flag; we *īmahe*, that is, we beg of him what we desire. (37)

O Agni, protect us; O God, ward off those who seek to harm us. Shatter our enemies, O you who are made of strength! 11 O Agni, protect us; O God, ward off those who seek to harm us. Shatter our enemies, O you who are made of strength! 11 O Agni, made of strength—that is, created by power—O radiant God, protect us from those who seek to harm us; "sma" is a filler particle. Shatter and rend asunder our enemies and those who hate us.

Agni, beautifying his own body with this ancient hymn of praise, the sage has grown great through the inspired singer. (12) Agni; with; this; hymn; beautifying; his own; body; the sage; with the inspired singer; has grown great. (12) The sage Agni, whose deeds are far-reaching, beautifying his own body—his very form—with this ancient, praiseworthy hymn, grows great through the inspired singer, the wise one who offers praise.

The mortal who honors the god Agni within his own home—for him alone does he shine forth wealth. (15) The mortal, that is, the human being, who in his home honors—that is, serves—the god Agni for the sake of attaining *tanvaḥ* (wealth); for *tanvaḥ* is listed among the names for wealth in the sense of "food" (*bhojanam tanā*). To him alone does Agni, shining brightly, bestow *vasu*, that is, wealth. He, Agni, grants it. (15)
1. [The verse beginning with] *tan-bhara-dvātāram*; [and] *bha1-3-māhātāram*. 2. The smoke-bannered flag:

"Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters. (16) Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth; this Agni quickens the seeds of the waters. (16) The head of the gods, the most excellent, the summit of heaven—the celestial world—loftily raised, and the lord of the earth: this Agni quickens the seeds of the waters, that is, all beings consisting of both the stationary and the moving, and thus he gratifies them.

O Agni, your pure, bright, and radiant rays rise upward; your lights are your flames. 17 O Agni! Your pure, bright, and shining rays—your lights, your flames—rise upward. O Agni, your pure, stainless, white-colored, blazing, and radiant rays, which are your lights and splendors, rise upward and spread forth.

For you, O Agni, are the lord of desirable wealth that leads to heaven; may I be your praiser under your protection. (18) O Agni, you are the master of desirable wealth that leads to heaven (*svarvati*); you are the lord of that which is to be chosen and given. On account of your protection—meaning for the sake of happiness—may I be your praiser. (18)

O Agni, the wise impel you with their thoughts; may our songs increase you. (19) O Agni, the wise—the masters of mind—impel you with their thoughts; the implication is that they praise you with hymns. Furthermore, they propitiate you alone with their mental acts. May our songs, our praises, increase you alone; may they cause you to grow.

We ever choose for ourselves the auspicious state of Agni—the undeceivable, self-sustaining messenger who ever praises [the gods]. (20) Of the undeceivable, of the self-sustaining, of the messenger, of the one who ever praises—of Agni, we choose the auspicious state. (20) O Agni, we ever choose the auspicious state of you who are undeceivable, unharmed by anyone; who are self-sustaining and powerful; the messenger of the gods; and who ever praises the gods. (39)

Agni, whose vows are most pure, the pure sage, the pure poet—pure, he shines when offered oblations. (21) Agni, whose vows are most pure (*śucivratatamaḥ*): one whose actions are exceedingly pure; *śuciḥ*: truly pure; *vipraḥ*: a wise sage; *śuciḥ*: pure; *kaviḥ*: a poet who has traversed all actions; *śuciḥ*: indeed pure; *āhutaḥ*: when offered oblations, Agni *rocate*: shines forth, becomes manifest.

And may my meditations and my songs increase you at all times, O Agni; be mindful of our friendship. (22) And indeed, O Agni, may my meditations—my ritual acts—and my songs—my hymns—increase you at all times. Be mindful of our friendship: that is, take note of our bond of friendship consisting of praise and other such acts.
1. The *tana* [syllables] are the *kakubh*. 2. The *gata* [syllables] are white in color.
[Maṇḍūkya Upaniṣad 8.6.44]

O Agni, you are indeed wise; for you, the inspired singer, sit consuming the oblations like one who guards the boundaries. You are ever watchful in promoting the welfare of all creatures, and you shine and play with the oblation in the mid-air. O Sage, O Vasu, prolong our life-span before calamities and before battles. O Agni, before calamities, before battles, O Sage, O Vasu, extend our life-span! 30.
O Agni, O Vasu, the dweller; O Kavi, the beloved one—protect us from misfortunes, from sins, and even before the onset of harms and destroyers.
That is to say, even before our enemies and misfortunes exert themselves to injure us. Prolong, that is, increase, our lifespan.

The third hymn consists of forty-two verses beginning with "ā ghā ye. Regarding this, the Anukramaṇikā states: "ā gha [ye]: forty-two verses; Triśoka is the seer; the first verse is addressed to Agni and Indra.
Because it is composed in the Anuṣṭubh meter, the seer is Kaṇva.
According to the technical rule (paribhāṣā), "The Gāyatra [is used] beyond the Vatsapra," the meter is Gāyatrī;
because it is an Anuṣṭubh [type], Indra is the deity.
However, for the first [verse], both Tvaṣṭṛ and Indra are the deities.
This hymn occurs in the *Gāyatra-aśīti* within the *Niṣkevalya* section of the *Mahāvrata*.
It is likewise prescribed in the fifth *Āraṇyaka*: "The two hymns beginning with ‘ā ghā ye abhimanyate’ and ‘ā tū na indra kṣumantam’" (*Aitareya Āraṇyaka* 5.2.3).
In the third round (*paryāya*), seventeen verses from the beginning of the *Acchāvāka-śastra* are recited.
Likewise, in the section on the *Atirātra*, it is prescribed in the Sūtra: "The seventeen [verses] beginning with *ā ghā ye abhiminyate*" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 6.4).
This verse, *ā ghā ye*, is the invitatory verse (*anu-vākyā*) for the *āmikṣā* offering dedicated to Indra.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "'*ā ghā ye abhiminyate*, *sukarmāṇaḥ surucaḥ devayantaḥ*—this is the hymn" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 2.9).
In the *atiriktoktha* of Maitrāvaruṇa, the six verses beginning with "astotram indrāya" are optionally used as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*.
This is stated in the Sūtra: "tad vo gāya sute sacā stotram indrāya gāyata" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 9.11).
In the second *paryāya*, for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the *stotriya* is the triplet beginning with "abhi tvā vṛṣabha."
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "O Bull, toward you at the pressing, [I call] with song toward the Lord of Cattle" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 6.4).
On the twenty-fourth day, at the morning libation, the *paryāsa-stotriya* for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is "Break asunder all [enemies].
And thus it is stated in the Sūtra: "‘Break asunder all enemies,’ [this is] for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 7.2).

Truly, those who meditate upon him and strew the sacrificial grass in succession—those whose friend is Indra, the youthful one. ā gha ye agnim indhate stuṇanti barhirānuṣak | yeṣāmindro yuvā sakhā ||1|| Truly, those who kindle Agni and strew the sacrificial grass in succession—those whose friend is Indra, the youthful one.
Those seers who indeed kindle Agni with preeminence, and for whom Indra, ever youthful, is a friend—they strew the sacrificial grass (barhis) in due succession.

Great is their impetus; abundant is their praise; wide is their sacrificial post—those whose friend is Indra, the youthful. (2) Great indeed is their impetus; abundant is their hymn of praise; broad is their sacrificial stake—for those whose friend is Indra, the ever-youthful. (2)
The great (bṛhat) and abundant (bhūri) praise (śasta) of these seers (ṛṣīṇām), as well as their sacrificial post (svaruḥ), is indeed vast (pṛthu).
The rest is self-evident.

This hero indeed drives away with his warriors the one who is hemmed in by battle—those whose youthful Indra is their friend. This hero indeed drives away with his warriors the one who is hemmed in by battle—those whose youthful Indra is their friend. (3)

Included among them, a certain one, being already a warrior by nature, though surrounded in battle by combatants—that is, by enemies—being himself a hero, he overcomes with his own forces; that is, he subdues the enemy.
1. Kha-ta-ma-śa-asi indeed you become.
2. Gha-ta-na-bha-kāṇva is the purifier.
3. Ta-na-ma-barhis.
Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 45. Sixth Aṣṭaka: 753.

Having taken up his arrow, the slayer of Vṛtra, as soon as he was born, asked his mother: "Who are the fierce ones? Who indeed are renowned? *ā bundaṃ vṛtrahā dande jātaḥ pṛcchaditi mātaraṃ | ke ugrāḥ ke ha śṛṇvire || 4 ||* "Born"—that is, having come into existence—"the slayer of Vṛtra," Indra, "took up" (*ā dade*) "his arrow" (*bunda*). Regarding this, Yāska says: "The *bunda* is an arrow" (*nirukta* 6.32). Having taken up the arrow, [he asked] "Who are the fierce ones"—those of formidable color and strength—and "who indeed are renowned" for their heroic power; thus he questioned his own mother.

Śavasī addressed you in response; like a beautiful elephant on a mountain, he who has provoked enmity toward you shall fight. O Indra, Śavasī, your powerful mother, spoke back to you. He who has cherished hostility toward you—he, like a beautiful elephant (*apsas*) upon a mountain, shall fight.

O Śakra, O Indra, may we, while entreating you, avoid your enemies—those who hate us—and not come near them. But rather, for the sake of receiving from you, who possess cattle and livestock, what we desire, may we go to you in full abundance. (43) Moving slowly, O wielder of the stone, we who possess horses, who possess hundreds of cattle, who are eloquent and free from distress, [may we approach]. (11) O wielder of the stone, O thunderbolt-bearer, moving slowly and gently, we who possess horses, who possess hundreds of cattle—that is, who have great wealth—who are eloquent, carrying what must be carried, and being free from calamity, may we go; such is the connection. (11) For upward indeed do your thousands and hundreds of pleasant gifts rise day after day, bestowing them upon those who sing your praises. (12) O Indra, for your singers—those who praise you—thousands and hundreds of upright, excellent, and pleasant means of success are bestowed day after day by the sacrificer. The root *mṛh* signifies the act of giving. (12) For we know you, O Indra, as the winner of wealth, the breaker even of the firm, the plunderer, like a house that protects from calamities. (13) O Indra, we know you as the conqueror of riches, the shatterer even of the strong enemies, the plunderer, and like a dwelling that guards against misfortunes. (13) O Sage, may the drops gladden you, even though you are already exalted; O Bold One, when we entreat you for the sake of gain. (14) O Sage, O Bold Indra, when we entreat you—the one who is being praised—from all sides for our desired object, then may the drops of Soma, though you are already exalted, gladden and exhilarate you. (14) Bring to us the wealth of that wealthy man who, though possessing riches, was ungenerous toward you and showed malice for the sake of granting us bounty. (15) O Indra, bring to us the wealth of that person who, despite being rich, was stingy toward you and harbored resentment for the purpose of giving us gifts. (15) These friends of yours, O Indra, who possess Soma, look upon you, O Indra, just as those seeking nourishment look upon their herd of cattle. (16) These companions of yours, O Indra, who possess the Soma juice, gaze upon you, O Indra, just as those who possess abundance look upon their livestock. (16) 1. gha-paṇimānāṃ | 2. ga-ta-bhara-kukuha cit; na-bha1-kukuha; bha3-kukuha ucchrita |
O Indra, these very friends of ours, the Soma-pressers who have prepared the juice—being well-nourished and having gathered their fodder—they look upon you as one looks at every single animal.

Moreover, we call you from afar here for protection—you who are not deaf, but possess hearing ears, being present [for our aid]. (17) Furthermore, O Indra, we, the Triśokas, call upon you from afar here at this sacrifice for protection—you who are not deaf, whose sense of hearing is unimpaired, and who are thus one with ears that hear. (17)

If you should hear this our invocation, then make it irresistible; moreover, be our closest kinsman. (18) If you should hear this our call, then make [our strength] unbearable for the enemies; and furthermore, be our most intimate friend. (18) O Indra, if you should hear this our invocation, then make [our power] difficult for the enemies to withstand; and also, be our nearest relative. (18)

For whenever we, afflicted by distress, have wandered about in poverty, O Indra, take heed of us as the giver of cattle. 19. For whenever indeed, O Indra, we—distressed by poverty and wandering about—have thought [of you], then take heed of us, thinking, "I shall be the giver of cattle to them. 19. *Api cit*: even; *he indra*: O Indra; *te*: to you; *yat*: when; *hi*: indeed; *vyathiḥ*: distressed by poverty; *jagvāṃsaḥ*: we who have wandered; *amanmahi*: we have thought; *tadā*: then; *naḥ*: of us; *godā it*: indeed the giver of cattle; *bodhi*: take heed, be aware.

O Lord of Power, we—the exhausted and aged—take hold of you as one takes hold of a staff; we desire you in the place of assembly. O Lord of Power, O Master of Strength, we—the worn-out and decrepit—seize you as the aged seize a staff for support. Thus says Yāska: "We take hold of you, as the infirm seize a staff" (Nirukta 3.21). Furthermore, we desire you in the *sadhastha*, that is, in the sacrifice.
